records.summary: ResourceDefinitionConverger is the resource convergence frontier from recognized headers and source metadata into compiler-consumable full definitions.
records.rationale: Resource convergence is one of the places where Aurelia's dynamic declaration shapes meet static product modeling. Future work on bindables, watches, aliases, template controllers, built-in resources, or compiler visibility should preserve this convergence step instead of folding full-definition construction into recognition or catalog admission.
guidance: Start here when a source-level resource header must become a FullResourceDefinition with exact provenance, alias claims, bindables, watches, and open seams.
Keep header recognition, definition convergence, and catalog admission separate unless framework.resource grounding shows a sharper boundary.

CustomElementConvergenceFrame is the per-custom-element read epoch inside resource-definition-converger.ts; it owns local-key prefixing, annotation priority, bindable/watch/template/dependency reads, and custom-element issue aggregation before ResourceDefinitionConverger publishes the final definition product.

ResourceDefinitionConverger now delegates source-field helpers to resource-convergence-support.ts, bindable metadata convergence to bindable-convergence.ts, and watcher metadata convergence to watch-convergence.ts. Custom elements include definition-object watches, decorators, and static Type.watches; custom attributes/template controllers intentionally ignore definition-object watches because runtime-html currently only merges decorator metadata and Type.watches for that resource family.

Watcher callback validation crosses from evaluator/static metadata into TypeChecker instance-member checks. Route those checks through TypeSystemProject's Program-node/runtime-target helpers; do not call checker APIs directly on convergence nodes that may not be Program-owned.

Use framework.resources pressure before changing definition provenance or treating header-level evidence as full-definition evidence; use `framework:resources -- --projection=convergence --detail` when the exact definition/backing/admission/materialization rows matter.
Use resource-source-address.ts for resource source spans and inline-template decoded-to-authored offset mapping; do not re-bury escaped-string coordinate logic inside ResourceDefinitionConverger.

For bindables, mirror runtime-html Bindable.getAll(Type): decorator metadata walks the class prototype chain base-to-derived, while static Type.bindables uses the nearest constructor static property. Do not generalize this inheritance rule to other resource fields without framework grounding.

Member @bindable(...) invocation follows runtime-html's property-decorator default-config path for known primitive/nullish/string arguments; keep the bindable and only leave an open seam for unknown or object-like values that may carry runtime config properties.

Class-level @bindable(...) runs through ClassBindableDecoratorFrame: string or object-with-static-string-name closes to a bindable, while bare/nullish/name-less configurations publish the framework-backed class-decorator configuration issues instead of becoming silent open seams.

Resource metadata annotations live in resource-metadata-annotations.ts: shared @alias(...) annotation values feed all named resources, while custom-element @containerless, @useShadowDOM(...), @capture(...), and member @children/@slotted registry dependencies feed full-definition convergence before definition-object and static class fallbacks.

Inherited metadata nodes belong to their declaring source file. Use ResourceRecognitionContextIndex/readNodeContext so imported decorator configuration is evaluated in the declaring module environment instead of the subclass module environment.

Resource source spans should use sourceFileAddressHandleForNode/readAdmittedNodeContext over contexts admitted by the resource-recognition pass. Do not re-resolve node source file names through KernelStore from resource convergence helpers.

Resource dependency uncertainty should carry resource-specific reason kinds through ConvergenceOpen and recordsForSourceOpenSeam. Vite-style `import.meta.env` optional dependency spreads should keep known dependency entries while reporting `resource-definition-dependencies-open`, not evaluator unsupported-expression noise.

Do not drop resource convergence open seams merely because the node cannot be mapped to an authored source-file span. Publish an addressless `resource.open-definition-field` seam with evidence and reason kinds so public open-seam rows can report the unresolved fact as unlocated rather than silently losing it.

Class-level @bindable overload reader and framework-backed issue publication path.
Watch metadata convergence from decorators, static watches, definition objects, and callback lookup.
Resource convergence source-address and inline-template source-map helper.
Resource metadata annotation reader for @alias, @containerless, @useShadowDOM, @capture, and @children/@slotted registry dependencies.

records.summary: Resource metadata diagnostics are owned by resource convergence and surfaced as ResourceIssue products with exact runtime-html error-code authority.
records.rationale: Aurelia's bindable decorator, processContent decorator, @children decorator, @slotted decorator, @watch decorator, and static/definition-object watcher metadata fail before template diagnostics owns anything. Static convergence can model malformed metadata and controller watcher callback lookup without opening the rendering or LSP layers, so these failures belong beside resource definition convergence rather than in API wording policy.
guidance: Start here when @bindable decorators, @processContent decorators, @children decorators, @slotted decorators, @watch decorators, static watches, custom-element definition-object watches, or controller watcher metadata produce framework-grounded diagnostics.
Use framework.errors usage rows before adding another ResourceFrameworkErrorCode member; AUR labels collide across packages and need exact package/enum/member authority.

Keep runtime-html invalid* partial through ResourceIssue products: AUR0227, AUR0229, AUR0766, AUR9989, and AUR9990 are modeled here. Runtime computed_not_getter / AUR0228 is an ObservationIssue, not resource convergence. AUR9991 is dormant in current framework source. AUR0769 and AUR0771 belong to app-root platform host state and Aurelia instance lifecycle state, not resource convergence.
Keep watch* complete through ResourceIssue products: AUR0772, AUR0773, and AUR0774 are modeled here.

Keep controller* ownership split across product substrates: AUR0501 is modeled as a resource-definition conflict, AUR0506 is modeled through watcher callback lookup, and AUR0507/AUR0508 are modeled by runtime controller observer setup after observer-locator branch/capability resolution. Lifecycle-state controller codes remain outside resource convergence.
Do not convert runtime-dependent watcher metadata into ResourceIssue rows. Leave those as typed resource convergence open seams until the evaluator or controller-state substrate can close them.

records.summary: Resource recognition publication owns target/source identity, resource identity, alias, attribute-pattern, and open-seam records for AST observations.
records.rationale: Recognition should stay kernel-light until the emitter/publication boundary. The README explicitly separates carrier recognition, kernel emission, publication support, and later definition convergence so headers remain a narrow bridge instead of becoming full resource metadata.
guidance: Start here when resource recognition needs target identities, TypeChecker-backed target types, resource identities, aliases, attribute-pattern identities, or recognition open seams.
Keep carrier recognizers and field readers out of kernel publication; use the emitter and publication support as the boundary.

Resource target type projection should stay lazy over members. Recognition publishes the target type reference and checker carrier; member enumeration belongs to expression access, diagnostics, completions, or authoring answers that explicitly need it.
Do not treat a recognized definition header as compiler-visible full metadata; converge it through ResourceDefinitionConverger when metadata matters.

anchors.summary: Resource recognition publication support.
Recognition emitter that frames source records, headers, products, and materialization records.
Resource recognition and convergence boundary notes.

records.summary: BuiltInResourceCatalogMaterializer owns framework resource catalog products, configured selections, and per-resource built-in publication.
records.rationale: Framework-owned resources enter semantic-runtime as concrete catalog/header/full-definition products, not as user-source recognitions. Built-in catalog grouping, configured catalog selection, and per-resource publication should stay separate so compiler-world visibility can prefer full definitions when available without losing admission/catalog provenance.
guidance: Start here when framework built-ins, configured resource catalogs, i18n/state/runtime-html/validation-html resource visibility, or built-in full definitions are involved.
Keep catalog grouping and configured catalog selection distinct from per-resource publication and built-in full-definition construction.

ValidationHtmlConfiguration admits a default validation-html catalog with ValidateBindingBehavior, ValidationErrorsCustomAttribute, and ValidationContainerCustomElement; option-sensitive subscriber toggles are still a future customization frontier.

Atlas resource convergence now sees nested framework definition calls such as CustomElement.define({ ...defaultContainerDefinition, template }, ValidationContainerCustomElement); use the convergence lens before assuming framework resources must be decorator/static-$au carriers.
Use `framework:resources -- --projection=convergence` and framework.discovery bundle rows before assuming StandardConfiguration is the only source of built-in resource visibility.

records.summary: ResourceRecognitionProjectPass remains the project-level orchestration boundary for shared evaluation, linked source and transform admission, source resource recognition, and full-definition convergence.
records.rationale: Resource recognition should not grow its own import resolver, build-tool inference, or one-source-only pass when external apps and plugins pull resources through linked source modules, assets, and admitted transforms. This project pass is the orchestration boundary from boot/evaluation/tooling facts into source recognition and convergence.
guidance: Start here when project-level resource recognition, linked source admission, build-transform admission, unresolved module carry-through, recognition profiling, or TypeChecker handoff changes.
Keep source-level recognizers and convergence materializers below this pass; this class should orchestrate them rather than learn carrier-specific resource logic.

Resource recognition depends on the shared project evaluator executing local side-effect imports. If a source file is admitted but its decorators are invisible, inspect StaticModuleGraphEvaluator.evaluateSideEffectImport before adding a resource-local import walk.

Convention-derived resources require source-specific transform evidence. Read supported build-tool configuration before recognition and publish an open admission seam when the transform cannot be closed; do not let recognizers infer project-global convention activation.
If imported templates lose exact provenance, inspect this pass and the shared evaluation source admissions before adding template-layer fallbacks.
When convergence follows AST nodes into linked modules, thread ResourceRecognitionContextIndex and ask readNodeContext for the owning source context before evaluating expressions or source spans.

anchors.summary: Project-level resource recognition and transform-admission pass.
Project tooling reader orchestrated before convention recognition.
Project-level recognition, linked-source, and transform-admission guidance.

records.summary: ResourceDefinitionIndex is the lookup surface from converged resource definitions back to evaluated values, target identities, products, dependency references, and resource names.
records.rationale: Later configuration, DI, compiler-world, and template materializers need to connect runtime/evaluator references to full resource definitions without rediscovering resource convergence. This index is the reuse point for those joins and should keep ambiguity explicit.
guidance: Start here when a materializer needs to resolve a resource from product handle, target identity, module/local name, dependency reference, resource name, or evaluated class/function value.
Resource-name lookup includes primary resource names and converged alias names; use it for template/compiler-world lookup instead of rebuilding consumer-local alias maps.

Router string routeables should use ResourceDefinitionIndex custom-element-only lookup and dependency-scoped custom-element lookup so parent component dependencies can disambiguate same-named resources without router-local maps.
Keep ambiguous local-name/resource-name lookups explicit; do not pick a definition by name when multiple definitions are visible.
If a new lookup path appears, add it to the index rather than adding local resource-definition maps inside DI, configuration, or template code.

anchors.summary: Converged resource definition lookup index.
Resource definition models, convergence, and compiler-world consumption.

records.summary: ResourceDefinitionApiIssueMaterializer owns direct runtime-html resource API failures that are provable from TypeScript source.
records.rationale: Direct CustomElementDefinition/CustomAttributeDefinition/ValueConverterDefinition/BindingBehaviorDefinition API calls are not renderer lookup failures and should not be diagnosed at the template API boundary. They are source-visible resource API paths that can be checked against recognized resource definitions and exact runtime-html framework error codes.
guidance: Start here when source calls to runtime-html definition create/getDefinition APIs need diagnostics.
Keep missing renderer resources in runtime controller/rendering issues and expression converter/behavior name misses in binding-utils/type-system lanes.
Use ResourceIssuePublisher for product records and exact framework-error authority; do not attach resource API diagnostics directly in AppDiagnostics.
Direct resource API issue sites carry boot-admitted source-file handles and publish spans through sourceSpanAddressForSite; avoid filename lookup for scanner-owned source diagnostics.
If a new direct resource API call shape appears, extend readResourceDefinitionApiCallSites or issueForResourceDefinitionApiCall before adding API-local checks.

anchors.summary: Materializes direct runtime-html resource definition API issue products.
Maps recognized resource definition API call sites to resource issues.
Resource issue product publication.
Runtime-html resource API framework-error grounding.

records.summary: cssModules and shadowCSS entries in custom-element dependencies are framework registry dependencies, not visible resource definitions.
records.rationale: Aurelia runtime-html exposes cssModules(...) and shadowCSS(...) as IRegistry values that component child containers register from CustomElementDefinition.dependencies. Resource lookup should not treat them as custom-element/custom-attribute resources, while app topology should still report their style assets.
guidance: When a resource dependency entry is a cssModules(...) or shadowCSS(...) call, classify it as a registry dependency rather than opening a resource-definition field seam.
When @children or @slotted appears on custom-element members, treat the generated lifecycle hook as annotation-backed registry dependency metadata, not merely as decorator diagnostics.
Keep registry dependencies out of ResourceDefinitionIndex visibility lookups; they affect registration/container semantics instead of resource-name lookup.
Use style-topology products to expose css-module, shadow-DOM, component stylesheet, and global stylesheet assets; do not duplicate style import classification locally in resource convergence.
Before extending style dependency semantics, re-check runtime-html styles.ts and custom-element dependency registration instead of assuming a component-like resource shape.

records.summary: Template controllers use custom-attribute registration identity and template-controller taxonomy.
records.rationale: Aurelia registers template controllers in the custom-attribute key space and branches on isTemplateController after attribute resolution. Semantic-runtime should mirror that framework model: public/editor rows may present template-controller as author-facing taxonomy, but resource joins, duplicate detection, dependency/container spending, and rename/reference declaration-to-usage matching must use registration identity.
guidance: Use registrationResourceKindFor(...) for framework registration-key joins; TemplateController maps to CustomAttribute and AttributePattern maps to null.

Use taxonomyResourceKindForDefinition(...) when presenting converged definitions to authors or editor surfaces; CustomAttributeDefinition with isTemplateController=true presents as TemplateController.

Do not make ResourceDefinitionConverger emit a separate full TemplateControllerDefinition merely to align usage and declaration kinds; the full runtime definition remains a CustomAttributeDefinition with isTemplateController=true.

Runtime keys are not taxonomy carriers: au:resource:custom-attribute:<name> can only prove custom-attribute registration identity unless a full definition or configured resource row supplies the template-controller flag.

Keep source form separate from both axes: @templateController(...), @customAttribute({ isTemplateController: true }), static $au, define calls, and conventions are declaration/provenance forms, not registration key spaces.

records.summary: Bindable property identity and public attribute aliases are separate rename/reference surfaces.
records.rationale: Aurelia bindable metadata has distinct configuration, TypeScript-symbol, callback, and public template-name surfaces. The runtime property name identifies the backing view-model field, while an optional attribute value is an independently authored public contract. References preserve all declarations and usages; property rename updates the property plus metadata and default-derived spellings but retains explicit aliases; alias rename remains a separate template-attribute operation.
guidance: Preserve field-specific metadata provenance for name, attribute, callback, mode, and set; keep propertyTarget and callbackTarget as separate TypeChecker-backed relations rather than treating a metadata token as the implementation declaration.
Publish authored metadata spans through the shared address/evidence/provenance helper so source handles and fieldProvenance name the same witnesses.
Template cursor members may have a scope-introduction source distinct from their reached TypeScript declaration source. Definition prefers the declaration; references and rename retain both.

Property references enumerate explicit-alias usages because they read or write the property, but property rename skips explicit aliases. Default-derived attribute spellings continue to derive from bindableAttributeNameForProperty(newName).
TypeScript-origin property propagation includes distinct bindable metadata names and default-derived template spellings while leaving explicit aliases stable.

Only default-derived nameChanged callbacks follow a property rename. Spend the converged callbackTarget and the shared TypeScript symbol enumerator; an explicitly authored callback name is an independent contract.

Observed dependency rows for a resolved scope member use the reached checker member declaration before slot provenance. Static bindable metadata remains a separate declaration row instead of masquerading as the observed symbol.
Alias references and alias rename use the bindable attribute source as their target and never acquire TypeScript reference edits.
Inline custom-attribute multi-binding aliases spend MultiBindingSegment.targetSourceAddressHandle for the segment target token; do not fall back to the enclosing value or primary bindable.

anchors.summary: Carries metadata field sources plus backing property and callback targets.
Converges field provenance and TypeChecker-backed member targets once at the resource boundary.
Keeps reached member declarations distinct from slot provenance in observation rows.
Builds shared references and rename closure from canonical property targets plus metadata declarations.
Publishes authored TypeScript source spans as address, evidence, and provenance records together.
Covers declaration forms, owner isolation, metadata/property closure, callback propagation, and exact field sources.

records.summary: Convention-derived resources require source-backed build-transform admission rather than class/file-shape inference.
records.rationale: Aurelia conventions are implemented by build-tool preprocessing that emits resource metadata before runtime registration. A convention-shaped source class is therefore not itself proof of a resource. Semantic-runtime must admit the transform from project tooling, preserve that evidence per matching source, and remain open when configuration cannot be closed statically.
guidance: Do not recognize convention resources from class/file shape alone; ResourceRecognitionProjectPass must supply source-specific transform evidence.
Read tooling configuration through the shared StaticProjectEvaluationPass with tooling-config roots and narrow host intrinsics; do not build a resource-local AST closure evaluator.

Carry Vite and Aurelia plugin factory identity through StaticModuleExternalValueResolver and the CommonJS require host boundary; do not reconstruct import identity from local syntax inside the resource adapter.
Use evaluator executedCallExpressions for plugin-call evidence; syntax-only scans must not turn uninvoked helpers or dead branches into transform admission or open seams.

Supported static Vite configuration reads @aurelia/vite-plugin admission, enableConventions, and include/exclude source filters through the same evaluator path for ESM imports/exports and CommonJS require/module.exports. Missing tooling or explicit false means the convention resource is absent.
Dynamic plugin lists, options, or filter expressions publish resource.open-convention-transform-admission instead of minting confident resource definitions.
Convention admission seams preserve evaluator boundary reason kinds such as host-environment-value instead of replacing known provenance with feature-not-yet-modeled.
Convention recognition provenance retains the tooling transform evidence and paired-template admission. A derived public resource name remains non-editable until an authored name token exists.

Webpack-loader, Gulp, Parcel, and ts-jest invoke the same preprocessor through different configuration carriers. Add explicit admission readers and pressure fixtures before claiming those carriers are covered; do not restore a project-global convention fallback.
Static Vite filters use the same @rollup/pluginutils/createFilter implementation as the framework plugin. Non-static filter values remain open rather than being approximated as closed.
